title: First violin and drums, then trumpet with Maurice Duran and Professor Nicholson
summary: No one else in his family played; he tried violin in 1913, then trap drums, then learned trumpet fingering from Maurice Duran and studied with Professor Nicholson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well, anyhow, back to your life and all I've kind of met, did your family play music in any way? No, no. I was the only one in the family that, uh,

took the music. And I started, I guess you'd like to know that, started trying to play a violin. And that was around in 1913. So I tried to play a violin when I kept it a couple of months with an instructor, somebody tried to show me. And I couldn't do anything with that. So then I changed my mind, and I got another instructor to show me how to play the trap drums. Mm-hmm. Because I liked that and thought I would do better. So I did do pretty good. I kept doing that for a couple of years. And something came up with this bus, trolley transportation. They didn't want you to ride on the street called the bass drum. Mm-hmm. So you'd have to hire a wagon to go everywhere you wanted to go and come back to it. And I couldn't afford that, because I didn't get enough money to do that. So then I had to leave that drums alone. And I had a friend in the band, who I was playing drums, was a trumpet player, which we just called his name, Maurice Duran. Oh yeah. He showed me the first finger, you know, of the trumpet. Then I got a teacher, tried to teach me how to play it. This man didn't play trumpet, but he played other instruments, see. And he showed me that. Do you remember his name? Yeah, his name was Professor Nicholson. Now the first name I don't know, Nicholson, that's all I can tell you. Was he in a certain school or something? No, he used to do this at his home. You know, he had quite a few scholars.
That must be Camille Nicholson's dad. Had a daughter named Camille? Probably so, probably.
He teach a lot of other musicians. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Well, I didn't know him, but I knew he had other scholars, quite a bit of other scholars there.
That's a famous family, that family. She's teaching there in Washington last year. Oh yeah.
She started the B-Shop music concert. So you started with the trumpet after 1913 then?
